request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary

Patient Name: [redacted]
Medical Record Number: [redacted]
DOB: [redacted]
Admission Date: [redacted]
Discharge Date: [redacted]

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted with complaints of headache and altered sensory perception. MRI images revealed gyriform enhancement with FLAIR hyperintensity and restricted diffusion in the right parietal cortex. The patient was found to have elevated protein and lymphocytic pleocytosis through CSF analysis. Additionally, the patient's glucose levels were elevated, and he was diagnosed with diabetes mellitus. The patient had spent significant time outdoors, including recent trips to Maine and New York, but had not reported any tick or mosquito bites. Serum was positive by JCV IgM ELISA with a PRNT of 1:160.

The patient remained in the hospital for observation and monitoring. The patient's headache and fatigue persisted over the next year, but repeat MRI 14 months later was normal. The patient was discharged with recommendations for outpatient follow-up appointments and further evaluation and monitoring as needed.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Follow-Up:
It is recommended that the patient follow up with a neurologist for ongoing evaluation and monitoring. The patient should also continue following recommendations for diabetes management.

Discharge Medications:
N/A

Discharge Plan:
The patient was discharged in stable condition with recommendations for outpatient follow-up appointments. The patient should continue following recommendations for management of diabetes. Further evaluation and monitoring is recommended for ongoing neurological symptoms.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The clinical picture is an encephalitis or meningoencephalitis. The serum is positive by IgM ELISA with PRNT 1:160 for "JCV," which here most likely stands for Jamestown Canyon virus. That fits the recent travel to Maine and New York (northeastern US), the outdoor exposure, and the CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis.

Jamestown Canyon virus is a mosquito-borne California serogroup orthobunyavirus. In ICD-10 it is coded under A83 (mosquito-borne viral encephalitis), and the California encephalitis group sits at A83.5, which is what the AM version would use for this. The alternative, A85.8 (other specified viral encephalitis), applies if the virus is not classified as mosquito-borne. Since Jamestown Canyon is mosquito-borne and in the California serogroup, A83 is the better fit.

The new diabetes diagnosis is a comorbidity, so it is not the principal diagnosis.

CODE: A83
